title: Debugging and Programming Challenge
summary: Apply systematic debugging (reading tracebacks, isolating the failing line, testing small pieces) to fix broken code under time pressure.
objectives: Read an error message to find the error type and the line number
Fix one bug at a time and run again after each fix

segments.title: What you will build today
segments.body:
## What you will build today

Today's program is already written, but it is broken in four places. Your job is not to write new code: it is to **debug**. Run the program, read the error from the bottom up (it tells you the error type and the line), fix that one line, and run again.

The four bugs are classics you will meet again and again: a `range` that stops one short, joining text and a number without `str()`, a line that is not indented under an `if`, and a variable name with a spelling mistake. Try to fix all four in about 15 minutes. As you go, write a short note about each bug in a list called `bug_log`, the way a real programmer keeps a bug log.

lab.title: Fix the four bugs
lab.objective: Use error messages to find and fix four bugs in a small score report, and keep a log of what you fixed.
lab.instructions:
The starter program should add up five scores and print a three-line report:

```
Total: 400
Good class
Average: 80.0
```

Right now it does not even run. It contains four bugs:

- a `range` that stops one short, so the last score is never added
- text joined to a number without `str()`, which causes a `TypeError`
- a line that is not indented under its `if`
- a variable name that is spelled wrongly

Fix them one at a time: run, read the error message (its type and line number), fix that line, run again. When the report is correct, fill the list `bug_log` with four short texts, one per bug, saying what was wrong and what you changed. Try to finish in about 15 minutes.
lab.constraints: Do not rewrite the program; fix the four lines. Keep the names scores, total, average and bug_log. The output must be exactly the three report lines. No input().
lab.starter_code:
# Score report. This program has FOUR bugs. Fix them one at a time:
# run it, read the error (its type and line number), fix that line, run again.
# The four bugs: a range that stops too early, a missing str(), a line that
# is not indented, and a variable name that is typed wrongly.

scores = [60, 70, 80, 90, 100]
total = 0
for i in range(4):
    total = total + scores[i]
average = total / len(scores)
print("Total: " + total)
if average >= 70:
print("Good class")
else:
    print("Needs work")
print("Average: " + str(avarage))

# 5. When all four are fixed, record each bug as a short text in bug_log (four entries)
bug_log = []
hints: Read the error message from the bottom line up: it names the error type and the line number. Fix only that line, run again, and read the next message. Four errors, four fixes.

range(4) gives 0, 1, 2, 3 and never reaches position 4, so use range(5) or range(len(scores)). Text can only be joined to text, so write str(total). The line under if ...: must be indented. Check every variable name letter by letter.

When the output is Total: 400, Good class, Average: 80.0, fill the log: bug_log = ["range stopped early", "missing str()", "print not indented", "avarage typo"]. Your own words are fine, but it needs four texts.

visible_examples.description: A TypeError and its fix: str() turns a number into text

success_criteria: Your program runs without an error and prints the report
total adds up all five scores (400)
The output is exactly the three report lines
bug_log holds four short texts, one per bug

tests.label: Your program runs without an error and prints the report
tests.remediation: Look at the error type and line number in the message, fix that line, and run again until no error is left.
tests.objective: Read a traceback and fix the failing line

definition.description: Runs and prints a non-empty report

tests.label: total adds up all five scores (400)
tests.remediation: range(4) only visits positions 0 to 3. Use range(5) or range(len(scores)) so the last score is added too.

tests.label: The average line reads Average: 80.0

tests.label: The output is exactly the three report lines
tests.remediation: Print only the three report lines: Total: 400, then Good class, then Average: 80.0. Join text to a number with str(total), and indent the print under the if.
tests.objective: Fix a TypeError and an indentation mistake

tests.label: bug_log holds four short texts, one per bug
tests.remediation: Put four texts in quotes inside bug_log, separated by commas: one note for each bug you fixed.

definition.expr: isinstance(bug_log, list) and len(bug_log) == 4 and all(isinstance(b, str) and b.strip() != '' for b in bug_log)

lab.solution:
scores = [60, 70, 80, 90, 100]
total = 0
for i in range(5):
    total = total + scores[i]
average = total / len(scores)
print("Total: " + str(total))
if average >= 70:
    print("Good class")
else:
    print("Needs work")
print("Average: " + str(average))

bug_log = [
    "range(4) stopped before the last score - changed to range(5)",
    "TypeError joining text and a number - wrapped total in str()",
    "print under the if was not indented - added four spaces",
    "avarage was a typo - changed to average",
]
